usual_baseline: Most patients are on medication: 81–96% [3043][3284][3288]. Antipsychotics over 4 weeks without psychosis 86% [3195]; 80% had no licensed indication, mean 36.79 months, with no physical review [3284]. Time-limited prescribing 39.4%, written information 4.2% [3288]. PRN over one week in 21 of 50 inpatients [3043].
fix_that_works: A trust prescribing guidance for personality disorder [3195] raised documented reasons for antipsychotics from 43% to 69% and medication reviews from 90% to 100%.
fix_that_fails: After the same guidance, antipsychotics over 4 weeks without psychosis rose from 86% to 91%, Z-hypnotics over 4 weeks from 13% to 37.5%, benzodiazepines over 4 weeks from 28% to 38%, and crisis plans fell from 87% to 79% [3195]. Review quality was unchanged.
consultant_advice: Only one loop is closed, and guidance alone did not cut long-term prescribing. Don't just count prescriptions. Audit whether antipsychotics are reviewed with a plan to stop, whether physical health checks happen, and whether patients get written information, which is almost never given.
